title: Protocol for culturing the endocrine junctional zone of the mouse placenta in serum-free medium
protocol: Cull the pregnant animal by cervical dislocation.
Sterilize the abdomen of the animal with 70% ethanol, blot dry with clean paper towel to remove excess ethanol.
Make a skin incision in the abdomen with blunt scissors and peel back the skin.
Use a new pair of blunt scissors and a pair of blunt forceps to open up the abdomen.
Remove the whole uterus and quickly submerge it in 50 ml ice-cold PBS in a Gosselin container, closing the cap.
Keep the container on ice during transport.
Separate individual implantations containing the embryo and placenta from the uterine horns under ice-cold PBS in a sterile dish.
Prepare a 35 mm dish containing ice-cold PBS for each implantation and leave it on top of the ice.
Rinse the uterine horns briefly in a 100 mm dish with ice-cold PBS to remove loosely attached material.
Separate the implantations from the uterine horns using fine scissors by cutting between each one.
Place each separated implantation in a separate 35 mm dish with cold PBS prepared previously.
Keep the dishes containing the implantations, amniotic sacs, and placentas on ice until further processing.
Dissect out the labyrinth region under a stereo-microscope.
Process one implantation at a time in the 35 mm dish in ice-cold PBS.
Carefully remove remaining uterine tissue enclosing amniotic sac and placenta using fine forceps.
Gently tear uterine tissue apart if necessary to access placenta.
Peel off decidua layer from basal surface of placenta using fine forceps, starting from the edge and gradually extending towards the center.
Hold placenta in position using amniotic sac as an anchor during peeling process.
Separate amniotic sac from placenta once decidual layer is removed.
Cut umbilical cord with fine forceps at the chorionic plate to minimize contamination of chorion/amnion.
Carefully dissect labyrinth from junctional zone using ultrafine forceps.
Lay placenta flat with chorionic surface and umbilical cord facing upwards for examination.
Use one forceps to gently hold the placenta.
Use another forceps to separate along the edge of the labyrinth.
Push closed forceps into the boundary between the labyrinth and junctional zone.
Allow forceps to open slowly to tease the tissue apart.
Continue separating around the disc perimeter.
Flip the placenta over after completing a round.
Lift up the edge of the junctional zone layer with one set of forceps.
Use another forceps to slowly tease apart the two layers towards the center until completely separated.
Clean up the dissected junctional zone by removing any remaining pink labyrinth tissue if necessary.
Transfer the junctional zone to a new dish containing pre-cooled DMEM/F12 medium.
Keep the junctional zone on top of the ice until step 2.
Dice the dissected junctional zone tissue into cubes approximately 1–1.5 mm3 in size using fine forceps inside an insert in dish containing the Jz-medium under the stereo-microscope.
Place the diced junctional zone tissue from one or two placenta in a Netwell™.
Transfer the inserts containing junctional zone explants into either a 12-well plate or a 6 well plate with medium.
Incubate the plate in a humidified 37°C incubator containing 5% CO2 and 10% O2 balance N2 for 48 h.
Add MTT (50 mg/mL) to the culture medium at a final concentration of 500 μg/mL to check viability after incubation.
After 48 h culturing, add MTT to the culture medium at a final concentration of 500 μg/mL.
Incubate in the incubator for 1 hour.
Collect junctional zone explant tissue from the inserts and place it in a 1.5 mL tube.
Snap freeze the tissue in liquid nitrogen for subsequent analysis (Western blotting, PCR etc).
Centrifuge conditioned medium at 4000 rpm (1771 g) for 30 minutes at 4°C to remove tissue debris.
Transfer the supernatant free of cell debris to a new tube.
Transfer clarified CM to a Vivaspin centrifugal concentrator for concentration according to the manufacturer’s instructions until desired volume reduction is achieved.
Transfer concentrated CM to a 1.5 mL tube and store both junctional zone explant tissue fragments and concentrated conditioned medium at -80°C until further analysis.
